critique: The black field, cyan-green palette, and centered radial expansion are aligned with a Ring Explosion. At 1.9s there is now a clearly particulate circular form, but it fills almost the entire frame and reads more like a turbulent spherical shell/wreath than a clean explosive ring. Dense internal webbing and bright clumped knots obscure the outward ring structure. At 0.08s the source is still a tiny, smooth bullseye rather than a brief burst of individually discernible particles.

suggestions.why: Reduce radial travel so the expanding ring remains comfortably inside frame at the later sample, preserving a readable circumference and center void.
Lower the burst density so the early source and later ring resolve as separate particles instead of smooth, opaque concentric bands and dense cloud-like webbing.
Reduce positional force influence to retain a broken explosive perimeter while suppressing the large turbulent internal ribbons and clustered knots.
